questions.prompt: Which flattening operator should you use for a typeahead search box?
questions.explanation: switchMap cancels the previous in-flight request when a new term arrives, so a stale response can't overwrite a newer one.

questions.prompt: Match each combination operator to its behavior.

pairs.right: Emit latest of each when any source emits
Wait for all sources to complete, then emit once
Emit on the primary stream, adding the latest of a secondary

questions.explanation: Each combines independent streams differently; picking the right one expresses the intended data dependency.

questions.prompt: Where should catchError usually be placed relative to a flattening operator, and why?

options.text: After the flattening operator, to catch everything at once
Inside the flattening operator's callback, so an inner failure doesn't terminate the whole outer stream
Before the flattening operator, on the source
It doesn't matter where it goes

questions.explanation: Placing catchError after the operator lets an inner error kill the outer stream permanently; inside it catches only that inner failure.

questions.prompt: When would you choose exhaustMap over switchMap?

options.text: For a live search where only the latest input matters
To ignore new triggers while an operation is in flight, e.g. preventing duplicate form submits
To run all requests in parallel

questions.explanation: exhaustMap ignores new source values until the current inner Observable completes — ideal for a Save button.

questions.prompt: Why prefer shareReplay({ bufferSize: 1, refCount: true }) over shareReplay(1)?

options.text: refCount: true tears down the source subscription when there are no subscribers, avoiding a memory leak

questions.explanation: The bare shareReplay(1) shorthand keeps the source alive forever; refCount cleans up when unused.

questions.prompt: Which @angular/core/rxjs-interop operator auto-completes a manual subscription when the component is destroyed?
questions.explanation: takeUntilDestroyed() replaces the manual Subject + takeUntil + ngOnDestroy cleanup boilerplate.
